entities.summary: Gérard Ernest Schneider was a Swiss painter born on April 28, 1896, in Sainte-Croix, who played a key role in the development of the lyrical abstraction movement and the School of Paris. This movement, which emerged in the 1920s, emphasized the expressive qualities of color and shape, influencing the development of modern art. Schneider's work, characterized by its use of vibrant colors and geometric forms, was exhibited alongside that of other prominent artists, including Pablo Picasso and Henri Matisse. Through his contributions to the movement, Schneider helped shape the course of modern art history. His legacy can be seen in the works of later artists who continued to explore the possibilities of lyrical abstraction. Schneider's paintings, which often featured bold, expressive brushstrokes and vivid color, continue to be celebrated for their beauty and emotional power. The School of Paris, which Schneider was a part of, was a major cultural force in the early 20th century, attracting artists and intellectuals from around the world. Schneider's work reflects the intellectual and artistic ferment of the time, as artists sought to break with traditional representations of reality and explore new ways of expressing the human experience.
